records.rawDisplayText:
I want to build a Linux systems knowledge base in this vault, similar in structure to my Java resource — a set of linked chapter notes I can keep expanding as I learn.

Create a new folder called Linux/ with an index note (Linux/00 - Index.md) that links out to individual chapter notes. Start with these chapters, each as its own note:

What is Linux — kernel vs. distribution, open source basics, how it differs philosophically from Windows/macOS
Distributions Overview — major distros grouped by purpose (beginner-friendly, stability-focused, power-user, enterprise, specialized), what distinguishes them
Core Parts of a Distro — the full stack: kernel, bootloader (GRUB), init system (systemd), system libraries (glibc), coreutils/shell, package manager, display server (X11/Wayland), desktop environment/window manager, filesystem hierarchy (/home, /etc, /usr, /var, etc.)
Essential Commands — core commands organized by category (navigation, files/dirs, viewing content, searching, permissions, process management, package management), plus how to discover new commands (man, --help, tldr, apropos)
The Unix Philosophy — small composable tools, piping, why the command line is central

For each chapter note: use clear headings, keep explanations practical rather than academic, include example commands in code blocks where relevant, and link related terms to each other using [[wikilinks]] (e.g. link "kernel" mentions across notes to a shared [[Kernel]] note if one exists). Tag each note with #linux.

Leave room in the index for me to add future chapters as I learn more (networking, permissions deep-dive, shell scripting, etc.) — don't try to cover everything at once.
